rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Concept 5: Connection between Minimum Deviation Condition and other topics  ·  Key Formula 5: Important relation in Minimum Deviation Condition  ·  ❌ At minimum deviation, the ray is perpendicular to both prism faces. ✅ At minimum deviation, the ray inside the prism is parallel to the BASE (for an isosceles prism), not perpendicular to the faces. The angles of incidence and emergence are equal but not necessarily 90°.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Any angle of incidence gives the same deviation. ✅ Deviation varies with angle of incidence. Only at one specific value of $i$ does the deviation reach its minimum. For other values of $i$, the deviation is larger.  ·  ❌ The angle of minimum deviation is zero for a prism. ✅ For a prism with $A > 0$ and $n > 1$, the minimum deviation is always positive. Zero deviation would require no refraction, which is impossible for a prism in air.  ·  ❌ Minimum deviation means the ray doesn't bend at all. ✅ "Minimum" means the smallest possible, not zero. The ray still bends — it's just the configuration that produces the least total bending.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ At minimum deviation, $r_1 \neq r_2$. ✅ At minimum deviation, $r_1 = r_2 = A/2$. This is one of the key conditions that defines minimum deviation.  ·  ❌ You can find δ_min without a spectrometer. ✅ While you can approximate δ_min with a simple setup, precise measurement requires a spectrometer to accurately measure the angle between incident and emergent rays.  ·  Note 3: Practice numerical problems regularly for mastery of Minimum Deviation Condition
